reason: The cited evidence (E1) concerns CoCrFeNiTix HEA coatings on Q235 steel, not the behavior of uncoated Q235 steel or its native passive film. It provides no support for the key premises about defect-driven passive film formation, surface modification effects, or chloride/temperature interactions on bare Q235 steel.
premises: Non-uniform passive film forms on Q235 steel due to microstructural defects
Defects like grain boundaries and inclusions create weak spots in the oxide film
Electropolishing and annealing can minimize surface defect density
Controlled mechanical deformation can increase surface defect density
Chloride ions and elevated temperature accelerate film breakdown at defective sites
